subject: Temporary APAC Data Routing & Subprocessor Objection Workflow
messages:
From: Mina Yamada <mina.yamada@asia-cloud.com>
To: naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: legal@asia-cloud.com
Date: 2027-07-20T08:12:00Z
Subject: Temporary APAC routing request + subprocessor list

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the quick onboarding call. As discussed, we need confirmation of (1) the subprocessors that may process AsiaCloud customer data if traffic is routed via your APAC edge for a temporary maintenance window, and (2) the objection window/process for any subprocessor additions relevant to APAC. Our security team wants the subprocessor names and the mechanism to register an objection within 30 days.

Can you send your subprocessor register and the proposed clause that governs temporary geographic routing (we called it a "doorway clause" internally)? We expect to route ~5–10% of traffic for up to 14 days.

Appreciate it — Mina
Mina Yamada
Legal Counsel, AsiaCloud
From: naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, soojin_lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, priya_natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-07-20T09:03:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Temporary APAC routing request + subprocessor list

Team — forwarding AsiaCloud's ask. Key points: they want the subprocessor register and clear objection path for APAC-temporary routing ("doorway"/temporary transfer). They expect a 30-day objection window and a capped routing period (~14 days).

Please see attached draft subprocessor list (Q2) and my initial suggestion for a short addendum clause. Karthik — can you confirm any material legal risk with a 14-day temporary routing? Priya — will this require an exec approval or procurement notification? Soojin — confirm which subprocessors are actually in APAC region and any data-export controls that might apply.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Privacy Operations Manager | Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, soojin_lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, priya_natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-07-20T10:23:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Temporary APAC routing request + subprocessor list

Naomi / team — quick thoughts:

- A 14-day window is reasonable from a risk perspective if we limit the routing to non-sensitive processing and keep logs for audit. We should explicitly exclude any regulated data classes (payment, healthcare, government IDs) in the temporary routing clause.
- For objections: AsiaCloud's 30-day window is standard; we should propose a two-stage process: (1) Notification (30 days) during which customer can object, and (2) If objection is raised, we either (a) remove the subprocessor for that customer or (b) offer additional controls/assurances. We should avoid a unilateral opt-out that breaks our ability to serve other customers.
- Ask infra to scope KV cache residency implications (will impact ability to route).

I'll redline the DPA to add a Temporary APAC Transfer Addendum and suggested language for objection escalation. Attaching DPA_redlines_v3.pdf.

Karthik
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: soojin_lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, priya_natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-07-21T02:15:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Temporary APAC routing request + subprocessor list

Naomi — attaching Subprocessor_List_Q2_2027.xlsx (filtered for APAC relevant parties). Short summary:
- APAC edge CDN: FastEdge Asia (subprocessor) — handles edge caching only (no persistent storage).
- Logging pipeline: StreamLog Ltd (Singapore) — transient logs retained for 7 days; can toggle retention for specific customers if required.
- Key management: We use central KMS in US; no APAC HSM at present.

Notes: FastEdge Asia and StreamLog are the only ones that would see routing-specific traffic. Both have standard SOC2 evidence; StreamLog retention can be shortened to 3 days for a customer-level restriction.

Soojin
Privacy Program Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Subprocessor_List_Q2_2027.xlsx
From: priya_natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
To: naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, soojin_lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-07-21T14:47:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Temporary APAC routing request + subprocessor list

Team — suggested operational workflow to send to AsiaCloud (short and action-oriented):

1) We will provide the APAC-filtered subprocessor list (attached).
2) AsiaCloud has 30 calendar days to object to any listed subprocessor for the temporary routing. An objection must be sent to legal@redwoodinference.com with a reason tied to the objection criteria in the DPA addendum.
3) If objection is received, we will respond within 5 business days with either (a) mitigation (reduced retention, config change), or (b) confirmation of removal for that customer.
4) Routing window: up to 14 days. If extended, requires a follow-up addendum signature via DocuSign.

I'll draft the short addendum text and a one-page notification email. Attaching our redlines to the DPA for review.

Priya Natarajan
Contract Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachment: DPA_redlines_v3.pdf
From: naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mina Yamada <mina.yamada@asia-cloud.com>
Cc: legal@asia-cloud.com, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, soojin_lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, priya_natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-07-22T09:05:00Z
Subject: RE: Temporary APAC routing request + subprocessor list

Hi Mina — attaching the APAC subprocessor list and our proposed Temporary APAC Transfer Addendum (redline attached). Summary:

- Subprocessors: FastEdge Asia; StreamLog Ltd (see attachment).
- Objection window: 30 calendar days from this notification. To object, please send an email to legal@redwoodinference.com with the subprocessor name and the basis for objection.
- Mitigation: If an objection is raised, we will propose mitigation within 5 business days (shorter retention or config lock). If mitigation is unsuitable, we will stop routing AsiaCloud traffic to that subprocessor for the duration of the routing window for your account.
- Routing cap: up to 14 days; extensions require an executed addendum via DocuSign.

DocuSign link for the addendum will be shared once we have confirmation there are no objections or once any open objections are resolved.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Privacy Operations Manager | Redwood Inference
Attachment(s): Subprocessor_List_Q2_2027.xlsx; DPA_redlines_v3.pdf
